clauses.text: A Sphere is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin outward in all directions.
The effect that creates a Sphere specifies the distance it extends as the radius of the Sphere.
A Sphere’s point of origin is included in the Sphere’s area of effect.

ambiguities.quote: specifies the distance it extends as the radius of the Sphere
ambiguities.reading_a: Distance from the origin is measured as true (Euclidean) 3D distance, so a 20-ft Sphere is round on the grid.
ambiguities.reading_b: Distance is measured with the grid movement count (each square, diagonal included, costs 5 ft), so a 20-ft Sphere covers a square block of squares on the grid.
ambiguities.proposed_ruling: Measure with the same distance metric the engine uses for range and movement on the grid (5 ft per square, diagonals included), so areas and ranges agree. A point exactly at the radius is inside.

ambiguities.quote: extends in straight lines from a point of origin outward in all directions
ambiguities.reading_a: A creature is in the Sphere when the centre of its space lies within the radius (as P-23/P-26).
ambiguities.reading_b: A creature is in the Sphere when any part of its space lies within the radius.
ambiguities.proposed_ruling: Use the centre of the creature's space, as proposed for Cone and Cube (P-23, P-26), so all areas follow one test.

ambiguities.quote: A Sphere’s point of origin is included in the Sphere’s area of effect.
ambiguities.reading_a: A creature whose space holds the point of origin (for example, a creature targeted as the centre of the Sphere) is affected like any other creature in the area.
ambiguities.reading_b: Only the point itself is part of the area; whether a creature at that point is affected still depends on the effect's wording.
ambiguities.proposed_ruling: Reading A: a creature whose space holds the origin is in the area and is affected if the effect affects creatures in its area. This is the opposite of P-25/P-27 for Cones and Cubes.

gaps.quote: from a point of origin outward in all directions
gaps.explanation: The unit doesn't say where a point of origin may sit on a grid: at a square's centre, at a grid intersection, or anywhere. This changes which squares a Sphere of a given radius covers (an even block from an intersection or an odd one from a centre).

traps.quote: A Sphere’s point of origin is included in the Sphere’s area of effect.
traps.note: The Sphere text matches 2014, but 2024 adds Emanation as a separate shape for effects that come from a creature (for example Spirit Guardians, which was a Sphere centred on you in 2014). If an implementation built from memory models self-centred auras as Spheres, the origin creature ends up in the area. Spheres include the origin; the Cone and Cube rules leave it out.

summary: Sphere has 3 clauses: it extends in straight lines in all directions from a point of origin, the effect sets its radius, and the point of origin is in the area. I was given no referenced units, so there are no relations or conflicts. The open questions are which distance metric to use and whether the edge counts, the inclusion test on a grid (centre of the space, as in P-23/P-26), and whether a creature at the origin is affected. Unlike Cone and Cube, a Sphere includes its origin. One gap: where the origin may sit on a grid. One trap: Emanation is new in 2024, so self-centred auras that were Spheres in 2014 are no longer Spheres.
